boards.title: Your First Weekend at Kalamazoo College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning campus landmarks, joining recurring student activities, exploring two downtown museums and resetting before class.

cards.title: Start at the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Hicks Student Center
cards.notes: Locate Student Development on the second floor, save Campus Safety’s number and use Hicks as your reference point for the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented inside the campus hub that houses key student services and recurring activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College locates Student Development in Hicks Student Center, second-floor East, Room 119, and lists Campus Safety among its student resources.
cards.source_title: Student Resources – Student Development | Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: Student Development lists weekday contact hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; Campus Safety is available 24/7 by phone.

cards.title: Learn the Dining-Hall Routine
cards.subtitle: Friday dinner · Second floor of Hicks Student Center
cards.notes: Walk upstairs to identify each station, check dietary labels and learn where to ask staff about ingredients before the first busy week.
cards.short_summary: Use the first dinner to understand the main dining hall’s layout and inclusive food options.
cards.evidence_claim: Welles is an all-you-care-to-eat dining hall on the second floor of Hicks Student Center, with buffet-style meals and dietary labeling.
cards.source_title: Kalamazoo College Dining Halls and Services
cards.access_notes: Meal-plan entry or payment is required; the official page says campus dining locations accept credit cards.

cards.title: Trace the Quad’s Landmarks
cards.subtitle: Friday early evening · The Quad
cards.notes: Walk one circuit while it is light, noting Hicks, Stetson Chapel and the academic buildings so tomorrow’s routes feel familiar.
cards.short_summary: Build a mental map from the named green at the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies the Quadrangle, or Quad, as the heart of campus and says it is bordered by academic and administrative buildings, the student center and Stetson Chapel.
cards.source_title: Campus Map for Kalamazoo College - About Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus stop; choose daylight and follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Try the Friday Rotation
cards.subtitle: Friday night · Usually Hicks Student Center
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar for this week’s format, bring your student ID and join whichever movie, game, craft or karaoke session is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: Meet people through a recurring Friday program whose activity changes each week.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Activities documents Friday Night Activities every Friday from 8–11 p.m., usually in Hicks Center, rotating among movies, games, crafts, karaoke and off-campus events.
cards.source_title: Programs and Events – Student Activities | Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: Current official hours are Friday 8–11 p.m., usually in Hicks Center. Check the calendar for location; student ID is used for event entry.

cards.title: Practice a Grab-and-Go Meal
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · First floor of Hicks Student Center
cards.notes: Use this stop to learn the to-go counter before a rushed weekday; confirm the day’s hours and available payment method before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Identify the campus counter for portable sandwiches, smoothies and yogurt bowls.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College says the Richardson Room is on the first floor of Hicks Student Center and prepares custom sandwiches, smoothies, yogurt bowls and other food to go.
cards.source_title: Kalamazoo College Dining Halls and Services
cards.access_notes: The cited page does not publish Richardson Room hours; verify the current dining schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Explore Kalamazoo’s Museum
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Downtown Kalamazoo
cards.notes: Allow time for all three floors, then use the exhibits to collect a few local-history reference points for future trips around town.
cards.short_summary: Add regional history, science and technology to the weekend without an admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum publishes Saturday public hours of 10 a.m.–4 p.m., offers exhibits and experiences on three floors, and states that general admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. General admission is free; some programs may charge fees. Visitors under 16 need an adult.

cards.title: Choose a Gallery Conversation
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Kalamazoo Institute of Arts
cards.notes: Pick one permanent-collection work and one special-exhibition work to discuss, leaving enough time to return before the galleries close.
cards.short_summary: Turn a downtown gallery visit into an easy shared conversation rather than a rushed survey.
cards.evidence_claim: The KIA is at 314 S. Park Street, opens Saturdays from 11 a.m.–5 p.m., and lists college-student admission for visitors 18 and older with ID.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit to the KIA
cards.access_notes: Saturday gallery hours are 11 a.m.–5 p.m. The KIA advises checking for changes caused by events, rentals or weather.

cards.title: Join the Saturday Night Series
cards.subtitle: Saturday night · Usually Hicks Student Center
cards.notes: Check the calendar for the theme and location, carry your student ID and arrive when the program begins instead of wandering campus late.
cards.short_summary: Close Saturday at the College’s recurring late-night activity series.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Activities documents Zoo After Darks every Saturday from 9 p.m.–midnight, usually in Hicks Center, with changing themes such as sports, competitions and performances.
cards.source_title: Programs and Events – Student Activities | Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: Current official hours are Saturday 9 p.m.–midnight, usually in Hicks Center. Check the calendar for the week’s location; bring student ID.

cards.title: Walk a Posted Arboretum Trail
cards.subtitle: Sunday daylight · 7787 West Main Street
cards.notes: Download the trail map before leaving campus, arrange transportation and complete a manageable daylight loop while following posted policies.
cards.short_summary: Use Sunday morning for a planned nature walk across the College’s public trail network.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College describes the Lillian Anderson Arboretum as a 140-acre natural area with five miles of trails, free and open to the public daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: Open every day from dawn to dusk. Follow posted policies, use the trail map and arrange transportation to the off-campus site.

cards.title: Set Up the Week at Upjohn
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Upjohn Library Commons
cards.notes: Find the circulation desk, save the current hours page and choose a study table for reviewing Monday’s schedule and organizing materials.
cards.short_summary: Finish the weekend by learning the library entrance, service points and Sunday access rules.
cards.evidence_claim: Upjohn Library Commons houses the Kalamazoo College Library; its current term schedule lists Sunday hours, and the building guide identifies study tables and the circulation desk.
cards.access_notes: Term schedules list Sunday hours, but summer and orientation weekends can be closed or reduced. Sunday term access requires a K College ID.
